new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Board reports ABSENT: no commodity claims it and no capture matches. It is not a spelling variant of anything already priced - bison is a distinct species sold at 2 to 3 times ground beef, so ground-beef-8020, any lean-beef id and any lamb id are all different price classes, not synonyms; the only word overlap ('ground') belongs to the cut, not the meat. If you reject, note the source line itself sanctions 'beef or lamb', so an existing lean ground beef id is the sanctioned human substitution rather than a silent bridge by me.

registrar_rulings.reason: Bison is unpriced anywhere in the estate and the estate already knows it is not beef: the only two 'bison' strings in all three namespaces are EXCLUDE patterns inside ground-beef-93-7 and ground-beef-9010 (commodities.json lines 55032, 55198), deliberately pushing bison products out of beef pricing; no id, label, floor-map pair, or smp-feed price cell carries bison, and the board's only 'buffalo' string is buffalo-wing-sauce, a condiment. Different species at a 2-3x price class = different purchase, not a variant of any ground-beef/turkey/pork id. Mint as RECIPE-ONLY (recipe-board baseline + recipe-commodities.json, not the weekly staples worklist). Prescription: include patterns anchored on the species word only - 'ground\s+bison', 'bison[^.]*ground', '\bbison\b(?=[^.]*(?:ground|lean))' - and do NOT include bare 'buffalo' (it collides with buffalo wing sauce and buffalo-style prepared foods); excludes need the full meat-commodity rigor (~150 patterns; copy ground-beef-93-7's exclude list and add 'buffalo', 'wing', 'sauce', 'jerky', 'sticks', 'burgers', 'patties', 'meatball'). Follow-up: add commodity-dupe-allowlist.json pairs ground-bison<->ground-beef-8020, <->ground-beef-93-7, <->ground-beef-9010, <->93-7-ground-beef, <->ground-turkey, <->ground-pork, reason 'different species, shared cut word ground', so audit-commodity-dupes.ps1 never pages Brad on the shared token. Separately, per the two-question rule: the ingredient NAME 'lean ground bison' needs its own vocabulary ruling (fdc:175293 Bison, ground, grass-fed, raw is the correct macros row for a raw purchase - use raw, not the cooked 173847); this id ruling does not mint that name.

macro_cross_check:
COUNTS. 12 residual lines ruled: 10 mapped, 2 not-purchased, 0 rejected. 21 buy strings written (all lines, settled included). 11 new food-DB rows returned, 0 declared absent. 2 new commodity ids proposed (ground-bison, fresh-dill); every other bid used is an existing live id and a reuse, not a proposal.

REJECTIONS AND REFUSALS. No line was rejected outright. Three form flips were refused rather than bridged: dried-dill for fresh dill (different price class, roughly tenfold gram difference per tablespoon), dried-parsley for the chopped fresh parsley, and any beef or lamb id for bison (different species and price class - the source's own '(beef or lamb)' is a cook's substitution, not evidence that the commodities are the same food). I also declined the shelf's Orange Zest -> orange-juice precedent for lemon zest: juice is not peel; zest comes off the fruit, so lemons prices it.

TWO LINES CARRY NO QUANTITY. Tzatziki and harissa are offered 'for serving' with no amount anywhere in the source, so both are not-purchased at 0 g. I supplied macro rows for both anyway so no food in this recipe is silent, but neither affects a number here. Read the harissa row's note before trusting it - its printed label rounds protein and fat to zero and will likely fail the Atwater gate; I left it as printed rather than reconstructing it.

CALLED OUT LOUDLY - THE CARB CEILING. This run's conditions say 35 g carbohydrate or less per serving. The source publishes 41.5 g and my independent recompute lands on 41.5 g, so the recipe is over the stated ceiling on a TOTAL carb basis and only clears it on a NET basis (roughly 38 g of fiber across the chickpeas, butternut, cauliflower and broccoli puts net near 32 g). The candidate pool banded it in with those exact published numbers, so an upstream gate has already seen 41.5 and admitted it. I am not rejecting a recipe whose macros reproduce the source almost exactly on a total-vs-net ambiguity, but a person should settle which basis the condition means, because this dish sits on the wrong side of it either way if the answer is 'total'.

LOWER-CONFIDENCE ITEMS, in order. (1) Chopped fresh dill at 2 g per tablespoon - dill fronds are feathery and published cup weights vary widely; 4 tbsp is 3.4 calories here, so the exposure is cost, not macros. (2) Breadcrumbs onto bread-crumbs, whose vocabulary name is 'Panko Breadcrumbs' - same commodity and price class, and I supplied plain-crumb grams (1 cup = 108 g) rather than letting a panko weight ride along, but a plain-form vocabulary name row is wanted. (3) The egg line lands mid-egg at 14 servings (3 1/2 eggs), so the buy string tells the cook to beat 4 and reserve about 2 tablespoons; that keeps the printed measure and the 175 g target in agreement instead of rounding to 4 eggs and silently adding 25 g.

The pre-resolve table was present, complete and looked right: 9 settled lines, 12 residual, evidence and FDC shelves attached per term, and the prior-rulings shelf capped at 4000 characters as advertised. I did not re-derive any settled line. Note the shelf's nearest neighbours for 'cauliflower florets' were flour, cranberries, carrot, large rolls and mushrooms - only the carrot ruling transferred (a knife cut is not a form flip), which is a fair example of cosine ranking wording rather than food.
